newsitem.title: CHINA: China voices anger at Japan war shrine visit.
newsitem.headline: China voices anger at Japan war shrine visit.

text.p: China lashed out on Thursday at a visit by Japanese members of parliament to a controversial war shrine in Tokyo this week, blasting the move as unacceptable and the worst form of provocation.
"With lawmakers obsessed with the country's militarist past, a further turn towards militarism is predictable in Japan's domestic and foreign policies," the official China Daily said in a commentary.
A group of 150 members of Japan's parliament, including two cabinet ministers, went on Tuesday to the Yasukuni Shrine.
"To visit the shrine is unacceptable," the China Daily said. To go there in an organised, large political group is provocation in its worst sense."

The Yasukuni is a Shinto memorial to the 2.6 million Japanese who have died in wars since the 19th century, including several executed Class-A war criminals such as General Hideki Tojo, who was prime minister during World War Two.
"This is indeed a dangerous move sure to invite condemnation from Japan's Asian neighbours, especially those who fell victim to Japan's atrocities during World War Two," the newspaper said.
It lashed out at Japan's bid for a seat on the United Nations Security Council, questioning what it called increasing Japanese arrogance in seeking a larger role on the world stage.
"The Japanese government has an inescapable responsibility for the situation," the commentary said of the shrine visit.
"Official connivance plays a major role in the wild resurgence of militarist tendencies in Japan," it said.
China has repeatedly expressed concern over what it sees as resurgent militarism in Japan, and accuses Tokyo of trying to whitewash its wartime atrocities.
China estimates up to 35 million Chinese were killed or wounded by invading Japanese troops from 1931 to 1945.
